SMTO-API-0001 — A step was rejected because its details were in the wrong form

GUID: fd4115ad-028c-4ad3-bb48-6889d1b10856
Slug: schema-validation-error
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • SMTO checks the details of every action before using them. A value was missing or in the wrong form, either something you entered or something the AI model filled in, so SMTO refused it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If this panel shows a Fields to correct list, change each listed value to match the description next to it, then save or send again. Those lines name the exact values SMTO couldn't accept, so fixing them clears this check.
  2. If this happened during a task, send your request again with more specific details, such as exact file names, folder names or numbers. The AI model builds each action's details from your words, and precise wording helps it fill them in the way SMTO requires.
  3. If the same step keeps being rejected, ask the person who manages SMTO to try a different model in Settings › Setup › Model routing. Some models follow SMTO's required formats less reliably, and resending the same request unchanged is refused the same way.

What success looks like

  • The value is accepted or the task step runs, and this message doesn't come back.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with a short note on what you were doing. Don't keep sending the same request unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A typed validation check (tool-argument JSON Schema, invalid tool-call arguments JSON, model structured output, or a runtime ValidationError) rejected a value as missing, mistyped or outside its constraints; tool-call rejections are returned with executed=false.

What this means

  • Typed/schema validation reports a field or tool-argument constraint failure; generic wrappers may also represent capability unavailability or an unvalidated structured response. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • Typed/schema validation reports a field or tool-argument constraint failure; generic wrappers may also represent capability unavailability or an unvalidated structured response.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owning validation stage, field and constraint before deciding whether caller input or an internal/generated response needs correction.

How to fix it

  • Read the field, constraint, expected and actual facts in Technical details (from ToolArgumentValidationError/SchemaValidationError, invalid_arguments_json or the structured-call diagnostics). Correct a user-supplied value at its source; for model-produced arguments, make the prompt more specific or switch the Main model in Settings › Setup › Model routing, and check the capability's arguments_schema if a valid call is being rejected.
  • Correct the field using the expected format in the technical detail, then submit again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual rejected contract validates while prior operation evidence remains intact.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
